title: Same cause, opposite directions
summary: Over South Asia and its seas (5 to 35 N, 60 to 100 E), the air 5 km up has warmed while the stratosphere 24 km up has cooled. Extra carbon dioxide does both: two heights, one cause, opposite trends.

finding.interpretation: From 1981 to 2025 the 500‑hPa air temperature over the 5°–35° N, 60°–100° E region rose by about 0.79 °C, corresponding to a trend of 0.176 °C per decade (0.018 °C yr⁻¹, 95 % CI 0.013–0.023 °C yr⁻¹) and a statistically significant p‑value of 2.4 × 10⁻¹¹. All four seasons show significant warming, with the strongest DJF increase of 0.251 °C per decade. Every one of the 140 grid cells exhibits a significant positive trend, indicating a coherent regional signal. The effect‑size metric of 2.75 suggests the observed change is large relative to natural year‑to‑year variability, pointing to potential climatic relevance.
finding.limitations: The trend is derived from the MERRA‑2 reanalysis, which incorporated a satellite sensor change (MSU/SSU to AMSU) in 1998‑1999 that could introduce artificial steps in upper‑air temperatures. Reanalysis uncertainties and the distinction between statistical significance and practical importance should be kept in mind when interpreting the results.
